title: Lin Fang v. Zhao Lei, private lending (fictional) · Loans and default

sources.name: Promissory note (first loan, 40,000 yuan)
sources.quote: On 4 March 2030 the borrower Zhao Lei borrowed RMB 40,000 from the lender Lin Fang (in words: forty thousand yuan; in figures: 40,000), for a term of one month, to be repaid by 4 April 2030.

sources.name: Promissory note (second loan, 40,000 yuan)
sources.quote: On 14 March 2030 the borrower Zhao Lei borrowed RMB 40,000 from the lender Lin Fang (in words: forty thousand yuan; in figures: 40,000), for a term of one month, to be repaid by 14 April 2030.

sources.name: Bank customer transaction statement
sources.quote: On 4 March 2030 the plaintiff transferred RMB 40,000 to the defendant by bank transfer.

sources.name: WeChat and Alipay transfer records
sources.quote: The plaintiff paid Xu Ying, a person not party to the case, RMB 34,000 by bank transfer and RMB 6,000 by WeChat transfer; Xu Ying then paid the defendant RMB 33,800 by Alipay transfer, RMB 2,000 by WeChat transfer and RMB 4,200 in cash.

sources.name: First-instance judgment in this case

loc.court: Example District People's Court, Example City, Example Province

sources.quote: After the two loans fell due the defendant repaid neither on time; this court supports the plaintiff's claim that the defendant repay the principal of the two loans, RMB 80,000.

events.label: Lin Fang transfers 40,000 yuan; Zhao Lei gives a note
events.detail: Lin Fang delivered RMB 40,000 by bank transfer; Zhao Lei issued a promissory note stating the amount, the term and the repayment date.

events.label: Zhao Lei borrows another 40,000 yuan via a non-party
events.detail: Because Zhao Lei said his bank card could not be used for the time being, Lin Fang, as instructed, transferred the money to Xu Ying (Lin Fang's daughter), a person not party to the case; Xu Ying then passed it to Zhao Lei by Alipay, WeChat and cash, and Zhao Lei issued a second promissory note.

events.label: First 40,000 yuan falls due, unpaid
events.detail: When the loan fell due Zhao Lei did not repay as agreed; neither loan's principal has been repaid.

events.label: Second 40,000 yuan falls due, unpaid
events.detail: The second loan was likewise not repaid at maturity; the court ordered Zhao Lei to pay overdue interest on each principal from its own maturity date at the LPR.
